newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh prisons like hell - report.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh prisons like hell - report.

text.p: Life in Bangladesh's jails is "almost like hell" due to overcrowding, torture and a complete lack of sanitation, a human rights group has said.
In many jails, four or five prisoners shared a space originally built for one, the Coordination Council of Human Rights said in a report received by Reuters on Monday.

"There is no practice of law in the jails. Extreme mismanagement, disorder, misbehaviour have crippled the jail administration. There are no sanitary facilities...and there are tortures," said the report, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Monday.
Home (interior) Ministry officials said there were about 45,000 prisoners cramped in the country's 78 jails which were built to hold a total of 21,620.
The human rights report said at least 70 people had died in jail riots, triggered by alleged maltreatment of prisoners, since Bangladesh's independence in 1971.
The human rights council attributed police brutality to the legacy of British colonial rule when Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan, was part of India from 1772 to 1947.
"When they (the British) used their own police at home to serve the people, they used police in their colonies as a tool for suppression," it said.
The report also said rape in (police) custody had created fear in the minds of women wanting to report crimes.
It said there were 11 reported cases of women being raped by law enforcement officers last year, compared to 30 in 1995.
"Many victims do not open their mouth for shame or fear. A young woman was detained by police for six days as she went to lodge a complaint against being raped," the report said.
